name: Snake plant
description: Snake plant care for Dutch homes: light, watering, winter placement, repotting and common problems for Dracaena trifasciata.
answer: Give a snake plant bright indirect light for its best growth, although it tolerates less. Let the potting mix dry well before watering again, use a draining pot, and keep it away from cold glass in winter.
light: Medium to bright indirect light; tolerates lower light with slower growth
water: Allow most or all of the mix to dry, then water thoroughly and drain
soil: Free-draining houseplant or succulent-style mix in a pot with holes
temperature: Normal warm indoor temperatures; protect from cold draughts
feed: Light feeding during active spring and summer growth
amsterdam: Its upright footprint suits narrow Amsterdam rooms, but a dim hallway is still not useful light. A position near a window usually produces firmer, faster growth than a decorative corner deep inside the room.
season: In a grey Dutch winter the pot may stay moist for weeks. Move it closer to daylight, stop watering by calendar and keep the leaves from touching cold glass.
propagation: Division is the quickest way to preserve a cultivar. Leaf sections can root, but variegated forms may revert to green.
safety: The plant can cause irritation if eaten and is a concern for cats and dogs. Keep it out of reach and check species-level veterinary guidance.
imageAlt: A flowering variegated snake plant in a large pot
mediaCaption: A flowering snake plant, supplied by Eve Plants.

name: ZZ plant
description: ZZ plant care in the Netherlands: realistic light, dry-down watering, winter care and common problems for Zamioculcas zamiifolia.
answer: Place a ZZ plant in medium to bright indirect light, let the potting mix dry substantially between waterings, and use a compact pot with excellent drainage. Lower light is tolerated, but growth becomes very slow.
light: Medium to bright indirect light; lower light is tolerated
water: Water deeply only after the mix has dried substantially
soil: Airy, fast-draining mix around thick rhizomes
temperature: Warm and stable; avoid cold windowsills
feed: Modest feed during visible active growth
amsterdam: The ZZ plant works well where floor space and attention are limited. Do not use its reputation for tolerance as permission to place it in a windowless corridor.
season: Short Dutch winter days slow an already measured growth rate. Keep the plant closer to useful light and expect a much longer interval between waterings.
signals: Often prolonged wetness; inspect the rhizomes
propagation: Divide established rhizomes when repotting. Leaf propagation is possible but slow and demands patience.
safety: All parts contain irritating compounds. Avoid sap contact and keep the plant away from children and chewing pets.
imageAlt: A dense table of houseplants at a Dutch garden centre
mediaCaption: Kamerplanten at a Dutch garden centre. Footage by Yoga and Plant With Roos.

name: Spider plant
description: Spider plant care for Dutch homes: light, water, brown tips, plantlets and winter adjustments for Chlorophytum comosum.
answer: Grow a spider plant in bright indirect or medium light, water when the upper mix begins to dry, and let excess drain. Give the arching leaves room and root mature plantlets when you want new plants.
light: Medium to bright indirect light; avoid abrupt harsh sun
water: Water after the upper layer dries; do not leave it standing in water
soil: Ordinary airy houseplant mix with good drainage
temperature: Comfortable indoor temperatures away from heat blasts
feed: Light, regular feeding while actively producing leaves and runners
amsterdam: A hanging spider plant uses vertical space in compact apartments. Keep it clear of a radiator and close enough to a window that its variegation stays strong.
season: Dry heated air and slower winter water use can happen together. Check the root ball at depth rather than reacting to every brown tip with more water.
signals: Uneven moisture, salt buildup or dry heated air
propagation: Peg a developed plantlet onto moist mix while attached, or cut it free and root it in water or mix.
safety: Spider plant is widely treated as a lower-risk choice, but discourage chewing and confirm suitability with a veterinarian for your own animals.
imageAlt: Hanging indoor plants at an Amsterdam garden centre
mediaCaption: Hanging plants at Intratuin Amsterdam. Footage by Yoga and Plant With Roos.

name: Rubber plant
description: Rubber plant care in Dutch homes: bright light, watering, stable placement, pruning and winter leaf drop for Ficus elastica.
answer: Give Ficus elastica bright indirect light, water after the upper mix has partly dried, and keep its position warm and stable. Clean the broad leaves and rotate modestly for balanced growth.
light: Bright indirect light; variegated plants need the brightest position
water: Water thoroughly after partial drying, then empty the outer pot
soil: Moisture-retentive but well-aerated mix in a stable pot
temperature: Warm, stable and away from draughts
feed: Balanced feed in active growth; little or none in winter slowdown
amsterdam: A rubber plant gives strong vertical structure without a wide canopy at first. Place it near tall apartment windows but leave space between foliage and cold glass.
season: Sudden autumn relocation plus reduced light can trigger leaf drop. Make placement changes gradually and reduce watering as the mix dries more slowly.
signals: Change in light, cold or root stress
Harsh sun, cold damage or watering extremes
propagation: Use stem cuttings or air layering. Wear gloves and protect surfaces from the milky latex sap.
safety: The latex sap can irritate skin and the plant is unsuitable for chewing pets or children.
imageAlt: A Dutch plant enthusiast holding a young rubber plant
mediaCaption: A young rubber plant in a Dutch home. Footage by Melissa Aarssée.

name: Peace lily
description: Peace lily care for Dutch apartments: useful light, even moisture, flowering, winter placement and brown-leaf troubleshooting.
answer: Keep a peace lily in medium to bright filtered light and water when the upper mix begins to dry, before repeated severe wilting. Use a draining pot and protect it from cold draughts and radiator air.
light: Medium to bright indirect light; brighter filtered light supports flowering
water: Aim for even moisture without constant saturation
soil: Airy, organic houseplant mix with drainage
temperature: Warm and draught-free
feed: Dilute feeding during active growth; excess can burn roots
amsterdam: Peace lilies can suit rooms that receive filtered city light, but a dark bathroom without a window will not sustain one. A bright bathroom can offer more stable humidity.
season: Move it away from a frequently opened winter window and monitor soil carefully; central heating can dry leaves while low light keeps roots wet.
signals: Dry mix, damaged roots or extreme temperature
Often low light or immature growth
Moisture swings, salts or dry air
propagation: Divide a mature clump so every section retains healthy roots and several leaves.
safety: Peace lilies contain calcium oxalate crystals and can cause oral irritation if chewed. Keep away from pets and children.
imageAlt: Indoor plants displayed in an Amsterdam plant shop
mediaCaption: Choosing plants in Amsterdam. Footage by Perfect Choice Nursery.

name: Heartleaf philodendron
description: Heartleaf philodendron care in Dutch homes: light, watering, climbing, pruning, propagation and winter care.
answer: Grow heartleaf philodendron in medium to bright indirect light, keep the mix lightly moist but aerated, and let the upper layer dry before watering again. Trail it or give it a support and prune sparse vines.
light: Medium to bright indirect light; tolerates lower light
water: Water after the upper mix dries slightly; reduce in winter
soil: Loose, organic and well-draining mix
temperature: Average warm indoor temperatures
feed: Modest feed during active growth
amsterdam: Its trailing habit makes use of shelves and tall ceilings without occupying much floor space. Keep it closer to the window than styling photos often suggest.
season: Growth slows sharply in low winter light. Move the plant closer to a window and lengthen the watering interval without allowing a cold, wet root ball.
signals: Wet roots or natural leaf ageing
Low light or lack of climbing support
propagation: Take stem cuttings with at least one node. Root in water or lightly moist mix, then combine several cuttings for a fuller pot.
safety: Calcium oxalate crystals make the plant irritating if chewed. Keep it away from children and pets.
imageAlt: Trailing houseplants hanging in a Dutch garden centre
mediaCaption: Trailing plants at Intratuin Amsterdam. Footage by Yoga and Plant With Roos.

name: Areca palm
description: Areca palm care for Dutch homes: bright filtered light, watering, humidity, brown tips and winter radiator protection.
answer: Place an areca palm in bright filtered light, keep the root ball evenly but not permanently wet, and protect the fronds from radiator heat and cold draughts. Give it space and inspect regularly for spider mites.
light: Bright indirect light with gentle sun after acclimation
water: Even moisture with drainage; allow slight upper drying
soil: Rich but airy palm mix in a pot with holes
temperature: Warm and stable, away from cold glass
feed: Palm-appropriate feed during active growth
amsterdam: Areca palms create a soft screen in larger living rooms but need more window light and floor area than a small nursery plant suggests.
season: Central heating can dry frond tips and encourage spider mites. Increase observation, not automatic watering, and measure humidity if damage continues.
signals: Dry air, salts or uneven moisture
propagation: Commercial pots often contain several seedlings. Division is possible but disruptive; seed propagation is slow.
safety: Do not treat a common name as a safety guarantee. Confirm the exact species with a veterinarian for pet-accessible rooms.
imageAlt: Tall houseplants lining an Amsterdam plant shop aisle
mediaCaption: Large foliage plants in Amsterdam. Footage by Perfect Choice Nursery.

name: Kentia palm
description: Kentia palm care for the Netherlands: light, watering, slow growth, winter placement and common frond problems.
answer: Give a Kentia palm medium to bright indirect light, a humus-rich draining mix and steady moisture without saturation. It is tolerant but slow-growing, so avoid repeated repotting and drastic changes.
light: Moderate to bright filtered light; avoid sudden harsh sun
water: Keep moderately moist while allowing drainage and some upper drying
soil: Humus-rich, well-drained potting mix
temperature: Comfortable indoor temperatures without draughts
feed: Infrequent, measured feeding during growth
amsterdam: Kentia palms have a long history as interior plants and tolerate less-than-perfect rooms, but their arching fronds need generous space and daylight.
season: Keep it away from radiator airflow and cold entrance halls. Slow winter growth means both watering and feeding should become more conservative.
signals: Dry air, salts or root stress
propagation: Kentia palms are grown from seed. Clumps sold together are separate seedlings, not offsets from one plant.
safety: Confirm the botanical identity and veterinary guidance if pets can chew the fronds.
imageAlt: A varied selection of indoor plants at a Dutch garden centre
mediaCaption: A Dutch garden-centre plant display. Footage by Yoga and Plant With Roos.

name: Boston fern
description: Boston fern care in Dutch homes: bright indirect light, moisture, humidity, winter heating and crisp-frond troubleshooting.
answer: Keep a Boston fern in bright indirect light with a consistently lightly moist, well-drained root ball and higher humidity. Protect it from radiator blasts and never let the whole pot dry hard.
light: Bright indirect light; some cultivars tolerate less
water: Maintain light, even moisture without waterlogging
soil: Organic, moisture-retentive and aerated
temperature: Cool-to-warm indoor conditions without extremes
feed: Dilute feeding during active frond production
amsterdam: A bright bathroom can suit Boston fern if it has a real window. A windowless bathroom is dark regardless of humidity.
season: Heated winter rooms can crisp fronds quickly while low light slows root use. Move away from radiators and monitor both humidity and soil rather than flooding the pot.
signals: Drought, dry air or root damage
propagation: Divide a healthy mature clump or separate rooted runners where present. Ferns also reproduce from spores, but that is a slower specialist project.
safety: Boston fern is commonly considered a lower-risk houseplant, but confirm pet-specific guidance and discourage chewing.
imageAlt: A collection of hanging foliage plants in Amsterdam
mediaCaption: Hanging foliage at Intratuin Amsterdam. Footage by Yoga and Plant With Roos.

name: Aloe vera
description: Aloe vera care in the Netherlands: sunny window placement, dry-down watering, succulent soil, winter care and offset propagation.
answer: Place Aloe vera at a very bright south- or west-facing window, acclimate it to direct sun, and let the mix dry completely before watering deeply. Use a small terracotta pot with several drainage holes.
light: Very bright light and several hours of acclimated sun
water: Let the mix dry completely, then soak and drain
soil: Coarse cactus or succulent mix with excellent drainage
temperature: Warm; protect from frost and cold wet conditions
feed: Very light feeding in spring and summer
amsterdam: Aloe needs one of the brightest places in an apartment. If neighbouring buildings block the sky, a windowsill may still be too dim in winter.
season: Dutch winter combines low light with cool glass. Keep the plant dry for longer, warm enough, and as close to strong daylight as possible.
propagation: Separate offsets once they have enough size and roots. Pot into a small dry mix and delay heavy watering while cuts settle.
safety: Leaf latex and whole-leaf ingestion can cause irritation or gastrointestinal effects. Keep away from pets and do not treat home-grown gel as medical advice.
imageAlt: Succulents displayed at a Dutch garden centre
mediaCaption: Succulents at a Dutch garden centre. Footage by Yoga and Plant With Roos.

name: Jade plant
description: Jade plant care for Dutch homes: sunny placement, dry-down watering, pruning, winter care and propagation for Crassula ovata.
answer: Keep a jade plant in a very bright window with gradually introduced sun, water only after the mix dries well, and use a heavy draining pot. Prune in active growth to shape the miniature-tree form.
light: Bright light with several hours of acclimated sun
water: Dry substantially between thorough waterings
soil: Gritty succulent mix in a stable draining pot
temperature: Warm growing season; cooler but frost-free winter is acceptable
feed: Light succulent feed during active growth
amsterdam: A sunny upper-floor window can work beautifully. A shaded ground-floor apartment between tall buildings usually needs a different plant or supplemental light.
season: Reduce water sharply when winter light and growth fall. Cold wet roots are far riskier than a short dry period.
signals: Drought or roots unable to absorb
propagation: Let clean stem or leaf cuttings callus, then place them on or in a lightly moist gritty mix under bright light.
safety: Jade plant can be harmful to cats and dogs if eaten. Keep fallen leaves and pots out of reach.
imageAlt: Compact succulent plants in a Dutch garden centre
mediaCaption: Compact plants in a Dutch garden centre. Footage by Yoga and Plant With Roos.

name: Wax plant
description: Hoya carnosa care for Dutch homes: bright light, flowering, dry-down watering, support and winter care for wax plants.
answer: Give Hoya carnosa bright indirect light with gentle sun, a small pot of loose fast-draining mix, and time to dry partly between waterings. Do not remove old flower spurs, because the plant can bloom from them again.
light: Bright indirect light with gentle acclimated sun
water: Allow partial drying, then water thoroughly and drain
soil: Loose epiphytic-style mix in a modest pot
temperature: Warm with no cold draughts
feed: Light feeding during active vine and bud growth
amsterdam: Hoya suits a bright shelf or hanging position, but its vines may eventually need a trellis. Place it where flowers and sticky nectar will not damage delicate surfaces.
season: Keep it close to winter light and avoid cold water or cold glass. Slower drying means a longer interval, not a permanently dry root ball.
signals: Light, maturity or repeated pruning of spurs
propagation: Take stem cuttings with nodes and root them in water, perlite or a light mix under warm bright conditions.
safety: Hoyas are often chosen for pet-aware homes, but verify the exact species and your animal’s risk with a veterinarian.
imageAlt: A collection of trailing waxy-leaved plants hanging in Amsterdam
mediaCaption: Trailing plants at Intratuin Amsterdam. Footage by Yoga and Plant With Roos.

name: Fiddle-leaf fig
description: Fiddle-leaf fig care in Dutch homes: strong window light, stable placement, watering, leaf cleaning and winter leaf-drop prevention.
answer: Place Ficus lyrata directly beside a bright window, water thoroughly after the upper mix partly dries, and keep light and temperature stable. Clean its large leaves and avoid oversized pots.
light: Very bright filtered light; acclimated gentle sun can help
water: Water after partial drying; soak evenly and drain
soil: Structured, well-aerated mix in a sturdy pot
temperature: Warm, stable and draught-free
feed: Balanced feed during active spring and summer growth
amsterdam: This plant needs more light than many interior photographs imply. Tall Dutch windows help, but place the canopy beside the glass rather than across the room.
season: Autumn light loss, moving the plant and turning on heating at once can trigger leaf drop. Change conditions gradually and keep roots from staying wet.
propagation: Stem cuttings can root, but air layering is often more reliable on an established woody stem. A detached leaf alone will not form a tree.
safety: Ficus sap can irritate skin and the plant is unsuitable for chewing pets.
imageAlt: A broad-leaved young Ficus plant being discussed in a Dutch home
mediaCaption: Broad-leaved Ficus care in a Dutch home. Footage by Melissa Aarssée.

name: Bird of paradise
description: Bird-of-paradise care for Dutch apartments: high light, watering, space, winter placement and realistic indoor flowering expectations.
answer: Give bird of paradise the brightest warm position available, including acclimated direct sun, water after the upper mix partly dries, and allow generous space for the leaves. Indoor flowering requires maturity and exceptional light.
light: Very bright light with acclimated direct sun
water: Regular in active growth after upper drying; less in winter
soil: Rich, structured and free-draining mix
temperature: Warm; protect from cold glass and draughts
feed: Regular balanced feed during strong growth
amsterdam: Large Strelitzia is often sold as instant interior architecture. Measure the window, ceiling, route upstairs and mature spread before bringing one into a compact flat.
season: Move it to maximum winter light and wipe broad leaves clean. Reduce watering as growth slows, but do not let an actively lit plant remain dry for extreme periods.
signals: Often normal movement damage; check draughts
propagation: Divide a mature multi-growth plant only when distinct rooted sections exist. Seed propagation is slow.
safety: Leaves and seeds can cause gastrointestinal upset if eaten. Keep away from pets and children who chew plants.
imageAlt: Large sculptural tropical foliage in an Amsterdam plant shop
mediaCaption: Sculptural foliage in an Amsterdam plant shop. Footage by Perfect Choice Nursery.

name: Flamingo flower
description: Anthurium care in Dutch homes: filtered light, airy soil, watering, humidity, flowering and winter radiator protection.
answer: Keep Anthurium andraeanum in bright filtered light, an airy epiphytic mix and steady warmth. Water after the upper mix begins to dry, drain fully, and protect leaves from radiator air.
light: Bright indirect light; avoid abrupt midday sun
water: Water after slight upper drying; never leave saturated
soil: Chunky, organic and airy epiphytic-style mix
temperature: Warm with moderate-to-higher humidity
feed: Dilute feed during active leaves and flowers
amsterdam: Anthurium can perform well near a bright east or west window. In deep rooms, colourful spathes fade and new growth becomes weaker.
season: Keep it away from a radiator and cold night-time glass. Lower winter growth requires less frequent water and little feeding.
signals: Dry air, salts or root stress
propagation: Divide established rooted growths during repotting. Stem sections with nodes can be rooted in warm humid conditions.
safety: Anthurium contains calcium oxalate crystals and can irritate the mouth and skin. Keep away from children and pets.
imageAlt: Colourful indoor plant displays in Amsterdam
mediaCaption: Indoor plant displays in Amsterdam. Footage by Perfect Choice Nursery.

name: Tradescantia zebrina
description: Tradescantia zebrina care for Dutch homes: bright light, purple colour, watering, pruning, propagation and winter refreshes.
answer: Give Tradescantia zebrina bright indirect light with some gentle sun, water after the upper mix starts to dry, and pinch or prune regularly. Root fresh node cuttings back into the pot when old vines become bare.
light: Bright indirect light; gentle sun deepens colour
water: Water after upper drying; avoid a constantly wet crown
soil: Light, ordinary draining houseplant mix
temperature: Warm and away from cold windows
feed: Light feeding during fast active growth
amsterdam: Its colour and quick growth suit a bright windowsill or shelf. It is inexpensive to restart, making it a good stekjes plant for neighbourhood swaps.
season: Winter growth can become pale and stretched. Move it closer to light, prune weak sections and use healthy spring cuttings for a dense reset.
signals: Age, low light or lack of pruning
propagation: Take short pieces with one or more nodes and root directly in lightly moist mix or water. Several cuttings make a fuller pot.
safety: Sap can irritate sensitive skin and may bother pets that chew it. Handle cuttings carefully and place out of reach.
imageAlt: Purple and silver Tradescantia plants at a Dutch garden centre
mediaCaption: Tradescantia and other compact plants at a Dutch garden centre. Footage by Yoga and Plant With Roos.

name: Dwarf umbrella tree
description: Dwarf umbrella tree care in Dutch homes: light, watering, pruning and winter care for Heptapleurum arboricola, formerly Schefflera arboricola.
answer: Grow dwarf umbrella tree in bright indirect light, water after the upper mix partly dries and prune in active growth to control height. Keep it warm and stable through winter.
light: Bright indirect light; green forms tolerate medium light
water: Water after partial drying and drain fully
soil: Airy, well-drained houseplant mix
temperature: Warm and protected from cold draughts
feed: Balanced feed during active leafy growth
amsterdam: The plant can become a compact indoor tree for a bright living room. Regular pruning keeps it proportionate to narrow rooms and stair access.
season: Expect slower growth and longer drying intervals in winter. Watch for scale and spider mites when central heating is running.
propagation: Root warm-season stem cuttings with several nodes in a light medium under bright filtered light.
safety: The plant contains irritating calcium oxalates. Keep it away from chewing pets and children.
imageAlt: Leafy indoor plants at a Dutch garden centre
mediaCaption: Leafy kamerplanten in the Netherlands. Footage by Yoga and Plant With Roos.

name: Yucca cane
description: Yucca cane care in Dutch homes: strong light, dry-down watering, stable pots, pruning and winter placement for Yucca gigantea.
answer: Put Yucca gigantea in a very bright position with acclimated sun, let much of the mix dry before watering and use a heavy draining pot. Low light plus frequent watering is the main indoor risk.
light: Very bright light with acclimated direct sun
water: Dry substantially between thorough waterings
soil: Coarse, free-draining mix in a stable container
temperature: Warm; protect indoor plants from cold wet roots
feed: Light feed during active growth
amsterdam: Yucca gives height without a very wide canopy, but sharp leaves need a safe traffic position. A bright top-floor window is usually a better fit than a shaded canal-house hallway.
season: Keep it close to winter daylight and dramatically reduce watering frequency as the pot dries more slowly.
propagation: Root healthy cane or stem sections in warmth. Basal offsets can be separated when they have enough growth.
safety: Yucca can be harmful to cats and dogs if eaten. Its pointed leaves also create a physical hazard in narrow walkways.
imageAlt: Tall architectural plants in an Amsterdam shop aisle
mediaCaption: Architectural houseplants in Amsterdam. Footage by Perfect Choice Nursery.

name: Christmas cactus
description: Christmas cactus care in the Netherlands: filtered light, watering, flowering cues, bud drop and propagation for Schlumbergera truncata.
answer: Grow Christmas cactus in bright filtered light and an airy mix, watering after partial drying rather than treating it like a desert cactus. Stable cool nights and long uninterrupted darkness help initiate buds.
light: Bright filtered light with gentle morning or winter sun
water: Water after partial drying; do not leave roots saturated
soil: Airy organic cactus mix suited to an epiphytic plant
temperature: Moderate warmth; cooler stable nights help bud formation
feed: Light feeding in the growth period, not during full bloom
amsterdam: A bright east window can suit it well. Once buds form, avoid moving it repeatedly between warm rooms and cold windowsills.
season: Autumn’s naturally longer nights can help flowering if artificial light does not interrupt darkness. Budded plants dislike abrupt temperature and moisture changes.
propagation: Twist off a short chain of healthy segments, let the end dry briefly and root it shallowly in a light mix.
safety: Generally considered lower risk, but eating plant material can still cause stomach upset. Confirm pet guidance with a veterinarian.
imageAlt: Compact succulent and epiphytic plants at a Dutch garden centre
mediaCaption: Compact plants at a Dutch garden centre. Footage by Yoga and Plant With Roos.

name: Moth orchid
description: Phalaenopsis orchid care in Dutch homes: window light, root-based watering, reblooming, repotting and winter cold protection.
answer: Keep a Phalaenopsis in bright filtered light, water when the exposed roots turn silvery and the bark approaches dry, then drain completely. Use orchid bark and never leave the crown full of water.
light: Bright indirect light with gentle morning or winter sun
water: Use root colour and bark dryness; soak and drain completely
soil: Open orchid bark, never ordinary dense potting soil
temperature: Warm with a modest day–night difference
feed: Weak orchid feed during active root and leaf growth
amsterdam: An east-facing window often gives a useful balance. Move the plant back from cold single glazing at night while preserving daytime light.
season: A modest autumn temperature drop can support spike initiation, but cold draughts damage tropical roots and buds. Winter watering intervals usually lengthen.
signals: Root rot or old collapsed tissue
propagation: Home propagation is uncommon. Occasionally a plant makes a keiki; separate it only after it has several leaves and developed roots.
safety: Phalaenopsis is widely regarded as a lower-risk orchid, but verify the exact plant and pet-specific advice before allowing access.
imageAlt: Flowering and foliage houseplants displayed in Amsterdam
mediaCaption: Choosing indoor plants in Amsterdam. Footage by Perfect Choice Nursery.
sourceName: Royal Horticultural Society: Phalaenopsis growing guide

name: Chinese evergreen
description: Aglaonema care for Dutch homes: medium light, watering, warmth, winter placement and colourful cultivar care.
answer: Keep Aglaonema in medium to bright indirect light, let the upper mix dry before watering and protect it from cold draughts. Colourful cultivars need more light than plain green forms.
light: Medium to bright indirect light; variegation needs more
water: Water after upper drying and drain fully
soil: Airy, moisture-retentive houseplant mix
temperature: Consistently warm and away from cold glass
feed: Light feed during active growth
amsterdam: Aglaonema tolerates filtered city light better than many colourful foliage plants. Keep it within the brighter half of the room rather than in a dark corridor.
season: Warmth matters in winter. A cold windowsill plus wet mix can damage roots even when the room feels comfortable during the day.
signals: Dry air, salts or moisture swings
propagation: Divide rooted clumps or take cane-like stem sections with nodes in warm conditions.
safety: Aglaonema contains calcium oxalates and can irritate if chewed. Keep away from children and pets.
imageAlt: Patterned tropical foliage in an Amsterdam plant shop
mediaCaption: Patterned tropical foliage in Amsterdam. Footage by Perfect Choice Nursery.

name: Dragon tree
description: Dragon tree care in Dutch apartments: light, watering, pruning, brown tips and winter care for Dracaena marginata.
answer: Give a dragon tree medium to bright indirect light, let the upper half of the mix dry before watering, and keep the canes warm. Prune a healthy cane in spring when you want branching.
light: Medium to bright indirect light
water: Allow substantial upper drying, then water and drain
soil: Well-drained houseplant mix in a stable pot
temperature: Warm and protected from cold draughts
feed: Light feeding in spring and summer
amsterdam: The narrow canopy works in compact rooms and corners, provided the plant still has a clear view of the window and enough space from passing coats and bags.
season: Reduce watering as winter growth slows. Keep the pot away from a cold entrance and the leaf tips away from radiator airflow.
signals: Moisture swings, salts or dry heat
propagation: Root top cuttings or healthy cane sections in warmth. The cut parent cane can produce new shoots below the cut.
safety: Dracaena is harmful to cats and dogs if eaten. Position fallen leaves and the plant out of reach.
imageAlt: Tall narrow houseplants in an Amsterdam plant shop
mediaCaption: Tall plants for compact homes, filmed in Amsterdam by Perfect Choice Nursery.
sourceName: NC State Extension: Dracaena reflexa var. angustifolia

name: Monstera
description: Monstera deliciosa care for Dutch homes: useful light, watering, climbing support, soil, winter adjustments and common leaf problems.
answer: Place Monstera deliciosa in bright indirect light, water thoroughly after the upper potting mix has partly dried, use a draining chunky mix and give mature stems a support. In Dutch winter, move it closer to light and expect slower drying.
light: Bright filtered light; gentle direct sun may be useful after gradual acclimation
water: Water thoroughly after the upper mix partly dries, then drain fully
soil: Airy, moisture-retentive but free-draining mix in a pot with holes
temperature: Warm and stable; protect leaves and roots from cold glass
feed: Moderate feeding during active growth; reduce when growth slows
amsterdam: Large leaves need useful daylight and room to climb. An east, south or west window with softened intensity usually works better than a decorative position deep inside an Amsterdam room.
season: In grey Dutch winter, move the plant closer to light and let the mix dry more slowly. Keep leaves away from cold glass, draughts and hot radiator air.
signals: Drainage, low light, pot size and root condition
Uneven watering, root stress, radiator air or accumulated salts
Plant age, light and climbing support
propagation: Take a stem cutting with at least one node and aerial-root nub. Root it in water or a light medium in warm, bright indirect light.
safety: Monstera contains calcium oxalate and can irritate if chewed. Keep it away from children and pets.
imageAlt: Monstera and hanging foliage in an Amsterdam garden centre
mediaCaption: Monstera and hanging foliage at Intratuin Amsterdam. Footage by Yoga and Plant With Roos.

name: Pothos
description: Pothos care for Dutch apartments: light, watering, pruning, propagation and winter adjustments for Epipremnum aureum.
answer: Grow Pothos in medium to bright indirect light, water after the upper mix dries, and use a pot with drainage. Trim sparse vines above a node and propagate node-bearing cuttings. Move it closer to a window in Dutch winter and reduce watering as growth slows.
light: Medium to bright indirect light; lower light is tolerated with slower, less variegated growth
water: Water after the upper mix partly dries, then soak and drain
soil: Ordinary airy houseplant mix in a draining pot
temperature: Warm and stable; avoid cold draughts and radiator blasts
feed: Light feeding during active growth
amsterdam: Pothos suits compact apartments as a trailing or climbing plant. Keep it close enough to a window that new growth stays leafy, rather than expecting a dark corner to sustain a full vine.
season: A Pothos several metres from a Dutch window may use water very slowly in winter. A brighter position is usually a better answer than stretching the watering interval indefinitely.
signals: Light, active-season nutrition and root space
Increase light gradually; genetics also matter
Low light, age or a need for pruning
propagation: Cut a healthy section with at least one node, the small joint where a leaf and aerial-root nub emerge. Root it in water or a lightly moist medium.
safety: Pothos contains calcium oxalate and is irritating if chewed. Keep it away from children and pets.
imageAlt: Trailing green houseplants hanging in an Amsterdam garden centre

name: Pilea
description: Pilea peperomioides care in the Netherlands: light, watering, rotation, repotting and how to separate and share Pilea pups.
answer: Keep Pilea in bright indirect light, water after the upper mix dries and rotate it regularly for even growth. Separate rooted pups only when they have their own small root system, then keep the new plants in stable bright light.
light: Bright indirect light; gentle morning sun can work after acclimation
water: Water after the upper mix dries; drain excess from the outer pot
soil: Airy houseplant mix in a pot with drainage holes
temperature: Warm and stable, clear of cold window glass
feed: Light feeding during spring and summer growth
amsterdam: A Pilea is ideal for a bright windowsill or table in a compact Amsterdam home. Rotate it a quarter turn occasionally so it does not lean toward one narrow source of light.
season: Short winter days slow growth and lengthen drying time. Keep the plant near useful daylight, pause routine feeding and avoid watering a cool, dim pot too often.
signals: Low light or limited nutrition during active growth
propagation: Separate a pup when it has several leaves and its own roots, or root a small offset in water or a lightly moist medium before potting it up.
safety: Pilea peperomioides is commonly treated as a lower-risk houseplant, but discourage chewing and check species-level veterinary guidance for your own animals.

name: Calathea
description: Calathea care for Dutch homes: filtered light, even moisture, humidity, water quality and winter care for Goeppertia houseplants.
answer: Give Calathea bright filtered light, an airy mix that stays lightly moist without becoming stagnant, and a warm position away from radiators and cold glass. Treat brown edges as a clue to investigate, not proof that tap water is the only cause.
light: Bright filtered to medium indirect light; avoid hot direct sun
water: Keep the mix lightly and evenly moist, letting excess drain; avoid both saturation and hard dry-outs
soil: Airy, moisture-retentive mix in a pot with drainage holes
temperature: Warm, stable indoor temperatures away from draughts
feed: Light feeding only during active growth; avoid frequent doses in low light
amsterdam: Prayer plants appreciate a stable position where radiator air, cold windows and sharp summer sun are not competing. In a compact home, a few steps back from a bright window is often better than a sill above a heater.
season: Dutch winter asks for less water, cleaner leaves and more attention to warmth. Keep the root ball from sitting cold and wet, and do not try to solve low light with extra feeding.
signals: Dry heated air, uneven moisture, salts, roots and pests
Root stress, drainage and cold conditions
Moisture, humidity, temperature and light changes
propagation: Divide a healthy established clump while repotting, keeping several stems and roots together in each division. Warmth and stable moisture help the divisions re-establish.
safety: Many Goeppertia species are treated as lower-risk for pets, but verify the exact plant and veterinary guidance for your household.

name: Baby rubber plant
description: Peperomia obtusifolia care for Dutch homes: bright filtered light, careful watering, compact growth and propagation.
answer: Keep Peperomia obtusifolia in bright indirect light, let a good portion of the mix dry before watering, and use a small airy pot. Its fleshy leaves store water, so frequent watering is unnecessary.
light: Bright indirect light; green forms tolerate medium light
water: Allow partial-to-substantial drying before watering
soil: Loose, airy and well-drained mix in a small pot
temperature: Warm and stable
feed: Light feed during active compact growth
amsterdam: Its small footprint makes it useful for a bright desk or sill. Keep it close enough to the window that new growth remains compact.
season: In winter the small pot may still dry slowly if the room is cool. Check below the surface and keep it from cold glass.
propagation: Root stem cuttings with nodes in a light mix. Leaf cuttings can work, though cultivar characteristics may vary.
safety: Peperomia is commonly chosen for pet-aware homes, but confirm the exact species and veterinary guidance for your household.
